recs.title: GPU-CFR: 80x Faster Counterfactual Regret Minimization by Compiling the Game to Static Dataflow and CUDA Graph Replay
recs.summary: GPU-CFR is proposed, a compiler and runtime built on observation that for a fixed game, everything about a CFR iteration except the numerical values is known before the first iteration runs, and beats every CPU and GPU baseline on the mid-to-large games of the suite without changing the update rule.

recs.title: Test-time Reinforcement Learning in Imperfect Information Games
recs.summary: This work extends the concept of gadget game, tabular technique for test-time search, to the reinforcement learning setting and formally proves that, unlike prior tabular algorithms, regularized policy-gradient algorithms limit possible strategy degradation caused by test-time reasoning, even without the gadget games.

recs.title: PokaiTrainer: Scaling Belief-State Search to Competitive Pok\'emon VGC
recs.summary: This work set out to build a strong VGC agent and report what that took, and found that on the live Showdown best-of-three ladder, the agent wins 59% of 150 sets against a human field averaging ${\sim}1320$ Elo.

recs.title: Abstraction Agent
recs.summary: The Abstraction Agent is proposed, a zero-shot pipeline that uses a large language model (LLM) to discover continuous strategic features from a natural-language game description, score private states on these features, and cluster them into abstraction buckets, without any game-specific evaluator, training data, or game-tree traversal during abstraction construction.

recs.title: Constant Individual Regret in General Games
recs.summary: This work introduces \emph{ECHO-OFTRL}: optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader (OFTRL) equipped with an EMA cascade for high-order optimism (ECHO), where EMA denotes exponential moving average, and leverages a new form of optimism inspired by modern filter design.

recs.title: NashDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
recs.summary: NashDreamer is proposed, a principled MBRL framework for two-player zero-sum IIGs that introduces a centralized Multi-Agent Recurrent State-Space Model (MARSSM) that decouples environment dynamics from the effect of players's strategies on their individual observations.

recs.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Policy Dynamics in Zero-Sum Networked Separable Markov Games
recs.summary: The entropy-regularized optimistic multiplicative weights update (ER-OMWU), a complementary single-loop policy dynamic that updates players'policies symmetrically and returns an approximate Nash equilibria in the last iteration, is proposed.

recs.title: Effective, Efficient, and General Information Abstraction for Imperfect-Information Extensive-Form Games
recs.summary: Experiments show that WEVA consistently outperforms equity-based and rank-based abstractions, reducing exploitability by up to over $80\% and establish WEVA as an effective, efficient, and general approach to information abstraction in imperfect-information extensive-form games.

recs.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
recs.summary: AV-AIVAT turns variance reduction into efficient, auditable early stopping while separating asymptotic screening from exact certification, so an evaluation can stop the moment its evidence suffices and hand a third party everything needed to recheck the verdict at that very stopping time.

recs.title: Real-Time Parallel Counterfactual Regret Minimization
recs.summary: Parallel CFR is presented, the first parallelization framework for real-time depth-limited CFR solving that seamlessly integrates pruning, abstraction, and advanced CFR variants and decomposes each CFR iteration into a pipeline of seven stages and identifies two orthogonal dimensions of parallelism.

recs.title: Agents That Certify Their Own Exploits: Confidence-Scheduled Restricted Responses for Safe Opponent Exploitation
recs.summary: CS-RNR is introduced, the first opponent-exploitation method whose safety guarantee is a certificate the agent computes on the strategy it actually deploys, so that every exploit it commits to is one it has audited itself.

recs.title: Superhuman AI for Stratego Using Self-Play Reinforcement Learning and Test-Time Search
recs.summary: This work establishes a step change in both performance and cost for Stratego, showing that it is now possible not only to reach the level of top humans, but to achieve vastly superhuman level -- and that doing so requires not an industrial budget, but merely a few thousand dollars.

recs.title: Look-ahead Reasoning with a Learned Model in Imperfect Information Games
recs.summary: An algorithm LAMIR is introduced that learns an abstracted model of an imperfect information game directly from the agent-environment interaction, and with sufficient capacity, it still learns a valuable abstraction, which improves game playing performance of the pre-trained agents even in large games.

recs.title: No-Regret Strategy Solving in Imperfect-Information Games via Pre-Trained Embedding
recs.summary: This paper proposes the Embedding CFR algorithm, a novel approach for solving strategies in IIEFGs within an embedding space that pre-trains information set abstractions via low-dimensional embedding for strategy solving, and is the first algorithm in poker AI that pre-trains information set abstractions via low-dimensional embedding for strategy solving.

recs.title: PokerSkill: LLMs Can Play Expert-Level Poker without Training or Solvers
recs.summary: The key finding is that rule-based skills alone do not constitute a strong strategy, and LLMs alone cannot play well, but their combination yields an agent that requires neither training nor solver access yet competes with systems built on millions of core-hours of computation.

recs.title: Parallelizing Counterfactual Regret Minimization
recs.summary: This paper presents a generalized parallelization framework, reframing CFR as a series of linear algebra operations, and describes how this technique can be applied to other tabular members of the CFR family of algorithms, including the state-of-the-art, such as CFR+, discounted CFR, and predictive variants of CFR.

recs.title: Correlated Chance Sampling for Monte Carlo Counterfactual Regret Minimization
recs.summary: Correlated Chance Sampling MCCFR (CCS-MCCFR), a drop-in replacement that assigns each concrete chance node a persistent randomized Weyl stream and maps its phases through the node's chance distribution, to establish unbiasedness along fixed strategy trajectories and isolate adaptive phase selection through a conditional scalar bound.

recs.title: Monte Carlo Sampling for Regret Minimization in Extensive Games
recs.summary: A general family of domain-independent CFR sample-based algorithms called Monte Carlo counterfactual regret minimization (MCCFR) is described, of which the original and poker-specific versions are special cases.

recs.title: Learning in games: a systematic review
recs.summary: The techniques used in these systems evolve from conventional search and learning to purely reinforcement learning (RL)-style learning methods, gradually getting rid of the domain knowledge.

recs.title: Regret Minimization in Games with Incomplete Information
recs.summary: It is shown how minimizing counterfactual regret minimizes overall regret, and therefore in self-play can be used to compute a Nash equilibrium, and is demonstrated in the domain of poker, showing it can solve abstractions of limit Texas Hold'em with as many as 1012 states, two orders of magnitude larger than previous methods.

recs.title: A Survey of Nash Equilibrium Strategy Solving Based on CFR
recs.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
recs.summary: The process of solving the strategy of Nash equilibrium based on CFR method is introduced and a conclusion of CFR-based methods and a prediction of future development are ended.

recs.title: DeepStack: Expert-level artificial intelligence in heads-up no-limit poker
recs.summary: DeepStack is introduced, an algorithm for imperfect-information settings that combines recursive reasoning to handle information asymmetry, decomposition to focus computation on the relevant decision, and a form of intuition that is automatically learned from self-play using deep learning.

recs.title: Refining Subgames in Large Imperfect Information Games
recs.summary: This work introduces the notion of subgame margin, a simple value with appealing properties that is guaranteed to find the optimal solution in subgame refinements resulting in large positive margins.

recs.title: Player of Games
recs.summary: The introduction of Player of Games, a general-purpose algorithm that reaches strong performance in chess and Go, beats the strongest openly available agent in heads-up no-limit Texas hold’em poker (Slumbot), and defeats the state-of-the-art agent in Scotland Yard, an imperfect information game that illustrates the value of guided search, learning, and game-theoretic reasoning.

recs.title: Heads-up limit hold’em poker is solved
recs.summary: It is announced that heads-up limit Texas hold’em is now essentially weakly solved, and this computation formally proves the common wisdom that the dealer in the game holds a substantial advantage.
